# Conservative Manifesto 2024: Summary

## Economy and Taxation
The manifesto proposes cutting employee National Insurance from 12% to 6% by April 2027, abolishing self-employed National Insurance, and introducing "Triple Lock Plus" to protect pensioner incomes from being taxed. Child Benefit would shift to household-based assessment, beginning withdrawal at £120,000 combined income. The party commits to not raising income tax, VAT, or corporation tax.

## Public Services
NHS spending would increase above inflation annually, with plans to recruit 92,000 nurses and 28,000 doctors. The manifesto proposes 250 new/modernised GP surgeries, 50 Community Diagnostic Centres, and expanded pharmacy services. Mental health support would expand in schools, with hubs for ages 11-25 in every community by 2030.

## Immigration
A legally binding annual cap on migration would be introduced, with Parliament voting on levels. The Rwanda removal scheme would continue, and illegal migrants would face removal. Visa fees would increase, and health checks for migrants would be introduced.

## Housing
The target is 1.6 million homes in England, with brownfield development prioritised. Stamp Duty exemptions for first-time buyers (homes up to £425,000) would become permanent, alongside a new Help to Buy scheme.

## Defence and Security
Defence spending would reach 2.5% of GDP by 2030. Support for Ukraine would continue. Police recruitment would add 8,000 neighbourhood officers.

## Energy and Environment
Annual oil and gas licensing rounds would continue alongside trebling offshore wind capacity and building Small Modular Reactors. The commitment to net zero by 2050 remains, with promises of no new green levies on household bills.

## Young People
Mandatory National Service for 18-year-olds would offer military placements or civic service. The manifesto proposes 100,000 new apprenticeships funded by closing underperforming university courses, plus the Advanced British Standard for 16-19 education.

## Transport
£36 billion from cancelled HS2 Phase 2 would fund local transport, including £8.3 billion for roads. The £2 bus fare cap would continue. The manifesto opposes road pricing and would reverse London's ULEZ expansion.
